clue.text: University material

definitions.meaning: one of the British universities founded in industrial cities in the late 19th and early 20th centuries
... is a building material, fired clay blocks of that colour

explanation.walkthrough: A redbrick university is a British term for the civic universities, as opposed to Oxford and Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: One word names both a class of civic English university and the reddish clay blocks such buildings were made from.

clue.text: A chronicle of revolutionary music

definitions.meaning: a written account of events, a history
a gramophone disc carries music and revolves on a turntable

explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' is not about revolt: a gramophone disc revolves.
explanation.definitionFit: The same word means a written account of events and a spinning disc holding sound.

clue.text: He was a natural selection as golf correspondent

definitions.meaning: Charles ... set out the theory of evolution by natural selection
Bernard ..., Charles's grandson, was for decades golf correspondent of The Times

explanation.walkthrough: Bernard Darwin wrote on golf for The Times from 1907 to 1953.
explanation.definitionFit: One surname belongs to the naturalist of evolution and to his grandson, a celebrated golf writer for The Times.

clue.text: With the confidence that comes from a new policy

definitions.text: With the confidence that comes from a new policy

parts.words: With the confidence that comes from a new policy
parts.note: read as ..., insured again under a fresh insurance policy, which gives confidence

explanation.surface: Someone feels secure after a change of plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'policy' is an insurance policy: someone covered anew is 're-assured', and so feels confident.
explanation.definitionFit: To be comforted and freed from doubt is to have one's confidence restored.

clue.text: No end of mice, thanks to this!

definitions.text: No end of mice, thanks to this!

parts.words: No end of mice, thanks to this!
parts.note: in the nursery rhyme Three Blind Mice the farmer's wife cuts off their tails with a kitchen blade

explanation.surface: A mousetrap or cat has caused countless mice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No end of' looks like 'countless', but means the mice lost their ends, their tails, as in the nursery rhyme.
explanation.definitionFit: The nursery rhyme has the farmer's wife cut off the mice's tails with a large kitchen blade for slicing meat.

clue.text: A bit of Switzerland in China

definitions.meaning: Switzerland is divided into administrative regions called ...
The old Western name for the Chinese city of Guangzhou

explanation.surface: A Swiss region turns up somewhere in China.
explanation.definitionFit: A Swiss state is a canton, and the southern Chinese port Guangzhou was long called Canton in English.

clue.text: How bizarre, to put the worker in charge !

parts.note: a worker is an ant, as in a worker ant

explanation.surface: How strange it is to put a worker in charge!
explanation.definitionFit: Antic as an adjective means grotesque or absurdly odd.

clue.text: Blue, red and white

parts.note: the colours of the French flag in order from the hoist

explanation.surface: A list of three colours.
explanation.walkthrough: These three colours in this order are the vertical bands of the French national flag.
explanation.definitionFit: A three-coloured flag, such as that of France, is called by this name.

clue.text: Maybe seek a man of the same calling

definitions.note: an adjectival phrase for a noun meaning a person with the same name

indicators.note: maybe says the letters could be arranged otherwise, signalling an anagram

explanation.surface: Perhaps go looking for a man in the same profession.
explanation.walkthrough: 'calling' looks like a profession, but here it means a name: someone called the same.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who bears an identical name to another, as if called the same.

clue.text: Tunes by French horns of Morgan & Co.?

definitions.note: Henry Morgan and his fellow buccaneers were pirates

parts.note: cor is the French word for horn, so cors are horns in French
airs are tunes or melodies

explanation.surface: Melodies played on French horns by a band called Morgan and Company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French horns' reads as the instrument but is the French word cor, plural; Morgan is Henry Morgan, the Welsh pirate of the Caribbean.
explanation.definitionFit: Corsairs are pirates or privateers, and Captain Henry Morgan led such a crew of raiders.

clue.text: Where the Roman host serves it with a rum cocktail?

indicators.note: a cocktail is a mixture of drinks, so these words are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: A Roman host pours drinks from a rum cocktail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cocktail' is the anagram signal: IT, A and RUM are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The atrium was the central hall of a Roman house, where guests were received and entertained.

clue.text: A retrospective artist in the spinster's collection.?

parts.note: facing back to the rear, the behind or bottom
a drawer is one who draws, an artist

explanation.surface: An artist's retrospective show is in an unmarried woman's collection.
explanation.walkthrough: A bottom drawer is the British term for the linen and household goods a young woman collected in readiness for marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: Household items a woman saved up before marriage were kept in a chest, a hope chest in American terms.

clue.text: A brace to every bit

parts.note: a horse's bit has a pair of leather straps fastened to it, one on each side, for the rider to steer with

explanation.surface: Every small piece comes with a pair of supports.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brace' means a pair and 'bit' is the metal mouthpiece of a horse's bridle, not a small piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Riding straps come as a pair, each one attached to a ring of the horse's mouthpiece.

clue.text: Club X has continental decoration

parts.note: an iron is a kind of golf club
the letter X is shaped like a cross

explanation.surface: A club for people marked X gives out a European medal.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a German military medal, and Germany is on the European continent.

clue.text: Greenery in some volume is sweet and sticky by the seaside

definitions.meaning: a book by the novelist Graham Greene, so a piece of Greene's work in one volume

definitions.text: sweet and sticky by the seaside
definitions.meaning: a hard stick of sugary candy sold at the seaside resort of Brighton

explanation.walkthrough: 'Greenery' is not foliage but writing by Graham Greene; Brighton is an English seaside resort whose rock is a stick of hard candy.
explanation.definitionFit: The title names both a Graham Greene novel and the striped stick of candy sold on the Sussex coast.

clue.text: One of Morpheus's forty ?

parts.note: Morpheus is the god of sleep, and forty winks is a nap, so one of them is a blink of the eye

explanation.surface: A question about one of forty things belonging to the god Morpheus.
explanation.walkthrough: Forty winks is a short sleep, and Morpheus is the god of dreams; the answer is the formal word for blinking.
explanation.definitionFit: Nictation is the act of blinking, and a wink is a single such closing of the eye.

clue.text: A song about America at the drinks party

indicators.note: the song wraps about the country

parts.note: a carol is a song
America gives USA

explanation.surface: A song about America is sung at a drinks party.
explanation.definitionFit: A carousal is a noisy drinking bout, a boozy revel.

clue.text: He may be of high or low degree

definitions.text: He may be of high or low degree

parts.words: He may be of high or low degree
parts.note: degree means an academic qualification, which may be first-class or a lower class

explanation.surface: A man may be of high or low social rank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of high or low degree' is an old phrase for social rank, but the degree here is a university award.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has completed a university course holds a degree of some class.

clue.text: Daedalian science that brought Daisy romance ?

indicators.note: the letters are brought round into a fresh arrangement, signalling an anagram

explanation.surface: A field of study that gave Daisy a love affair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought' signals the anagram of DAISY and ROMANCE; Daedalus of Greek myth built wings to fly.
explanation.definitionFit: Daedalus made wings and flew, so the science of air flow over flying bodies is fittingly his.

clue.text: Like the bachelor making one run ?

definitions.meaning: in cricket a hit that scores one run

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a hit scoring one run is called by this word.
explanation.definitionFit: Unmarried describes a bachelor, and in cricket one run scored off a stroke has the same name.

clue.text: Principal ingredient in a Wonderland kitchen

definitions.text: Principal ingredient in a Wonderland kitchen

parts.words: Principal ingredient in a Wonderland kitchen
parts.note: in Alice's Adventures in Wonderland the Duchess's cook fills the kitchen and soup with too much of a sneezy spice

explanation.surface: A recipe question about the main ingredient used in a fantasy kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: In Lewis Carroll's book the Duchess's kitchen is so full of this spice that everyone sneezes.
explanation.definitionFit: The Duchess's cook in Carroll's story seasons everything heavily with this spice, which makes Alice sneeze.

clue.text: Aged nudist in the Railway Museum ?

definitions.text: Aged nudist in the Railway Museum ?

parts.note: old means aged
a nudist goes about in the buff, so is a buffer

explanation.surface: An elderly naturist turns up among the exhibits of a railway museum.
explanation.walkthrough: An old buffer is British slang for a fusty old man, and a buffer is also the sprung end-stop on a railway vehicle, likely to be found among a museum's old stock.
explanation.definitionFit: An elderly fellow is slangily an old buffer, and a railway museum shows antique shock-absorbing buffers.

clue.text: Down in the mouth with a hangover

definitions.text: Down in the mouth with a hangover

parts.words: Down in the mouth with a hangover
parts.note: a fleshy flap literally hanging down at the back of the mouth, over the throat

explanation.surface: Someone feels miserable after a night's drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Down in the mouth' means sad and 'hangover' suggests drink, but it is a part that hangs over, down in the mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: The small fleshy lobe dangling from the soft palate at the back of the throat.

clue.text: Quick drink about four

indicators.note: the drink goes about, round, the number

parts.note: ale is a drink, a kind of beer
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Have a quick drink at about four o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quick' is the old sense of living, as in 'the quick and the dead'.
explanation.definitionFit: Quick in its old sense means living, as in the phrase about the quick and the dead.

clue.text: The wonder was, it was Zeus's!.

definitions.text: The wonder was, it was Zeus's!.

parts.words: The wonder was, it was Zeus's!.
parts.note: one of the Seven Wonders of the ancient world was the great ivory and gold figure of the god at Olympia

explanation.surface: Someone marvels that something belonged to the king of the gods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wonder' is not surprise but one of the Seven Wonders of the World, the figure of Zeus at Olympia.
explanation.definitionFit: The sculpted figure of Zeus at Olympia was counted among the Seven Wonders of the ancient world.

clue.text: Having to get out of 'bed for confession?

parts.note: owning means having
to be up is to be out of bed

explanation.surface: Someone must rise from bed to go to confession.
explanation.definitionFit: Admitting a fault is the act of confessing to it.

clue.text: General method of getting Jack's drift

definitions.note: Jack is Jack Tar, a sailor, whose drift is a ship's sideways movement downwind

parts.note: Robert E. Lee was the Confederate general in the American Civil War
a way is a method

explanation.surface: A general's way of grasping what a man called Jack means.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drift' looks like gist or meaning, but Jack is a sailor and the drift is a ship's sideways slide away from the wind.
explanation.definitionFit: In sailing, a vessel's sideways drift off course downwind is its leeway.

clue.text: What magnificence from a penniless undergrad!

indicators.note: the answer is made out of, from, the letters of the student word, reworked
without a penny, so the D, the old abbreviation for penny, is dropped

explanation.surface: A poor student shows unexpected splendour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penniless' removes D (the old British penny, from Latin denarius) from UNDERGRAD, and 'from' signals the anagram of the remaining UNERGRAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Grandeur is splendour or impressiveness, the quality of something on a magnificent scale.
